papers.title: Engineering the Interface: Nanodiamond Coating on 3D-Printed Titanium Promotes Mammalian Cell Growth and Inhibits
papers.abstract: Additively manufactured selective laser melted titanium (SLM-Ti) opens the possibility of tailored medical implants for patients. Despite orthopedic implant advancements, significant problems remain with regard to suboptimal osseointegration at the interface between the implant and the surrounding tissue. Here, we show that applying a nanodiamond (ND) coating onto SLM-Ti scaffolds provides an improved surface for mammalian cell growth while inhibiting colonization of Staphylococcus aureus bacteria. Owing to the simplicity of our methodology, the approach is suitable for coating SLM-Ti geometries. The ND coating achieved 32 and 29% increases in cell density of human dermal fibroblasts and osteoblasts, respectively, after 3 days of incubation compared with the uncoated SLM-Ti substratum. This increase in cell density complements an 88% reduction in S. aureus detected on the ND-coated SLM-Ti substrata. This study paves a way to create facile antifouling SLM-Ti structures for biomedical implants.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及SLM钛植入体的表面涂层，但缺乏力学测试和应力遮挡分析，与研究方向关联较弱。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not include mechanical testing (fatigue or static), stress shielding analysis, or porous structure design; it focuses solely on surface coating effects on cell growth and bacterial inhibition.

summary_en.motivation: To enhance osseointegration and antibacterial properties of additively manufactured titanium implants.
summary_en.method: Nanodiamond coating applied to selective laser melted titanium scaffolds.
summary_en.result: The coating increased mammalian cell density and reduced Staphylococcus aureus colonization.
summary_en.validation: In vitro cell viability and bacterial adhesion assays.

papers.title: Quantitative characterization of 3D bioprinted structural elements under cell generated forces.
papers.abstract: With improving biofabrication technology, 3D bioprinted constructs increasingly resemble real tissues. However, the fundamental principles describing how cell-generated forces within these constructs drive deformations, mechanical instabilities, and structural failures have not been established, even for basic biofabricated building blocks. Here we investigate mechanical behaviours of 3D printed microbeams made from living cells and extracellular matrix, bioprinting these simple structural elements into a 3D culture medium made from packed microgels, creating a mechanically controlled environment that allows the beams to evolve under cell-generated forces. By varying the properties of the beams and the surrounding microgel medium, we explore the mechanical behaviours exhibited by these structures. We observe buckling, axial contraction, failure, and total static stability, and we develop mechanical models of cell-ECM microbeam mechanics. We envision these models and their generalizations to other fundamental 3D shapes to facilitate the predictable design of biofabricated structures using simple building blocks in the future.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了3D生物打印微梁在细胞力作用下的力学行为，但未涉及任何AI方法。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not incorporate AI or machine learning into any stage of the bioprinting workflow; it focuses solely on experimental mechanics and analytical modeling. No validation is relative to AI-driven bioprinting.

summary_zh.motivation: 探究细胞力驱动下3D生物打印结构件的变形与失效机理
summary_zh.method: 打印含细胞的微梁，嵌入微凝胶培养基，观测力学行为并建立力学模型
summary_zh.result: 观察到屈曲、收缩、失效及静态稳定，并建立了细胞-ECM微梁力学模型
summary_zh.validation: 通过实验观测不同参数下的力学行为验证模型

summary_en.motivation: To establish fundamental principles of how cell-generated forces drive deformations, instabilities, and failures in 3D bioprinted constructs.
summary_en.method: 3D printed microbeams composed of living cells and extracellular matrix were embedded in a packed microgel culture medium to provide a mechanically controlled environment.
summary_en.result: Buckling, axial contraction, failure, and static stability were observed, and analytical mechanical models of cell-ECM microbeam behavior were developed.
summary_en.validation: Experimental observations of beam mechanics under varying beam and medium properties validated the proposed mechanical models.
